newsitem.title: FRANCE: Comoros politician suggests France leave Mayotte.
newsitem.headline: Comoros politician suggests France leave Mayotte.

text.p: A leading Comoros opposition politician has suggested that France should hand over the island of Mayotte, which has a higher living standard that has provoked a wave of secessionist protests in two other islands in the archipelago.

Prince Said Ali Kemal, a former finance minister, said in an interview published on Friday that demands by protesters' on the islands of Anjouan and Moheli to return to French rule would cease if Mayotte became part of the independent Indian Ocean archipelago.
"There would be no problems on Anjouan if Mayotte was not there," Kemal, a former ambassador to Paris and the grandson of the Comoros' last sultan, told the French daily Le Monde.

Mayotte was the Comoros' only island to choose to remain under French rule in a 1975 independence referendum. Secessionists on the impoverished islands of Anjouan and Moheli say independence mostly benefits the main Grande Comore island, and envy Mayotte's relative prosperity.

Kemal said there could be revolutions on all Comoros islands unless young people regained hope for a better future. Many residents of Anjouan and Moheli say independence has brought only poverty, civil strife and coups.
"Recolonisation would not be in France's or the Comoros' interest. On the contrary we must move towards reintegrating Mayotte in the future," he said.

France has given no indication it is considering relinquishing control over Mayotte. It has rejected demands for a return of Anjouan and Moheli to French rule and welcomed a mediation attempt by the Organisation of African Unity (OAU).
OAU envoy Pierre Yere of Ivory Coast is due to visit the Comoros next weekend and talk to both sides.
Comoran President Mohamed Taki has proposed giving the islands more autonomy to try to defuse the crisis.
